questions.q: What shift does the summary recommend for ambitious leaders?
a: Build ladders for others instead of only climbing your own
Avoid mentoring anyone until you retire
Compete with your team for promotions
Change jobs every few years to stay fresh
questions.why: Lesson 1 says exceptional leaders mentor rather than just advance themselves.

questions.q: What should you look for in people you mentor?
a: Hunger to learn and real potential to lead
Loyalty to your ideas and long tenure
High test scores and quiet manners
Personal friendship and shared hobbies
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to choose people who say they will find a way.

questions.q: What did Pat Summitt do at halftime that impressed Maxwell?
a: She let the team discuss first, then listened to their report
She gave a long motivational speech to the players
She replaced several of the starting players
She left the room to review game footage alone
questions.why: Lesson 2 says she connected with players instead of directing them.

questions.q: What does Maxwell write on his notepad during meetings?
a: A large letter L to remind himself to listen
Three goals for the conversation
The names of everyone present
A question mark beside each decision
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the letter helps him listen more than he speaks.

questions.q: Where does real influence come from, according to the summary?
a: Trust built by keeping promises, not from a title
The size of the budget you control
The seniority of your office location
The number of people who report to you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Claude's integrity mattered more than Maxwell's position.
